✧ The expedition of al-Khandaq took place in Shawwāl of the year five.
✧ Jewish leaders from Banū al-Naḍīr and Banū Wāʾil went to Quraysh, inciting them to war and claiming Quraysh's religion was better, prompting the revelation of Qur'anic verses.
✧ The same Jewish delegation went to Ghaṭafān of Qays ʿAylān, urging them to join the war against the Messenger ﷺ and informing them of Quraysh's support.
✧ Quraysh under Abū Sufyān, Ghaṭafān under ʿUyaynah b. Ḥiṣn, al-Ḥārith b. ʿAwf, and Misʿar b. Rukhaylah advanced against the Muslims.

✧ Upon hearing of the confederates, the Messenger ﷺ ordered a trench dug around Madinah, working alongside the believers while hypocrites slipped away and sincere Muslims briefly excused themselves for necessities.
✧ God revealed verses distinguishing faithful believers who ask permission before leaving from hypocrites who slip away from the trench work.
✧ While digging the trench, the Muslims chanted rajaz verses about Juʿayl, whom the Prophet ﷺ renamed ʿAmr, and he echoed their words.

✧ Miracles occurred during the trench digging: a hard rock crumbled after the Prophet ﷺ sprinkled water on it, dates and a small ewe fed multitudes, and flashes foretold conquests of Yemen, Syria, the West, and the East.
✧ Ibn Umm Maktūm was appointed over Madinah, and the Prophet ﷺ ordered that women and children be placed in the strongholds.
✧ Ḥuyayy b. Akhṭab persuaded Kaʿb b. Asad of Banū Qurayẓa to break his covenant with the Prophet ﷺ, promising to share his fate if Quraysh and Ghaṭafān withdrew.
✧ The Prophet ﷺ sent Saʿd b. Muʿādh, Saʿd b. ʿUbādah, and others to investigate Kaʿb's betrayal; they reported the treachery through a veiled allusion to ʿAḍal and al-Qārah.
✧ Fear and hardship intensified among the Muslims, while hypocrisy surfaced through remarks by Muʿattib b. Qushayr and requests for leave by Aws b. Qayẓī.
✧ The Prophet ﷺ considered ceding a third of Madinah's dates to Ghaṭafān, but Saʿd b. Muʿādh and Saʿd b. ʿUbādah rejected the idea, erasing the draft agreement and choosing war.

✧ Horsemen from Quraysh, including ʿAmr b. ʿAbd Wudd, ʿIkrimah b. Abī Jahl, Hubayrah b. Abī Wahb, and Ḍirār b. al-Khaṭṭāb, armed themselves, rode past the Banū Kinānah, and marveled at the trench as a stratagem unknown to the Arabs.
✧ Salmān al-Fārisī is credited with advising the trench, and the Prophet ﷺ declared him as one of the ahl al-bayt in response to competing claims from the Emigrants and Helpers.
✧ ʿAlī b. Abī Ṭālib challenged and killed ʿAmr b. ʿAbd Wudd in single combat after ʿAmr refused his call to Islam, and composed verses about the deed though their attribution is doubted.
✧ Ḥassān b. Thābit lampooned ʿIkrimah b. Abī Jahl for throwing down his lance and fleeing from ʿAmr, comparing his flight to an ostrich and his neck to a hyena cub's back.

✧ The Muslims' battle-cry was 'Ḥā Mīm, they will not be helped,' and Saʿd b. Muʿādh was wounded by an arrow shot by either Ḥibbān b. Qays, Abū Usāmah al-Jushamī, or Khafājah b. ʿĀṣim, leading to his prayer regarding Qurayẓah.
✧ Ṣafiyyah bt. ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib killed a Jewish man who was circling the fortress of Fāriʿ after Ḥassān b. Thābit refused to do so, citing his admitted cowardice.

✧ Nuʿaym b. Masʿūd, having secretly become Muslim, deceived the Banū Qurayẓah, Quraysh, and Ghaṭafān into mutual suspicion by advising each side that the others would betray them, thereby sowing discord.

✧ Dissension between Quraysh, Ghaṭafān, and the Banū Qurayẓah intensified over hostages, and a violent wind destroyed the polytheists' camp, prompting Abū Sufyān to order departure after Hudhayfah's reconnaissance mission.
✧ It recounts Gabriel's command to fight Banū Qurayẓa, the expedition from Madinah, their arbitration and slaughter, division of spoils, revealed verses, death of Saʿd b. Muʿādh, and martyrs.
✧ Gabriel, appearing to the Prophet ﷺ, conveys God's command to march against Banū Qurayẓa, and the Muslims are ordered not to pray ʿaṣr except at their fortresses.

✧ Ibn Umm Maktūm is appointed over Madinah, ʿAlī is sent ahead, the Prophet ﷺ besieges the Jews, and the section records the counsel of Kaʿb b. Asad, the repentance of Abū Lubābah, and the conversions and departure of certain men.
✧ Banū Qurayẓa submit to the judgment of the Messenger ﷺ, and the wounded Saʿd b. Muʿādh is appointed arbiter, ruling that their men be killed and women and children taken captive.
✧ The captured men of Banū Qurayẓa are beheaded in trenches in Madinah, including Ḥuyayy b. Akhṭab and Kaʿb b. Asad, with one woman executed; some individuals are spared through intercession.
✧ The Prophet ﷺ divides the spoils of Banū Qurayẓa, allotting shares to cavalry and infantry and taking a fifth, and later he keeps Rayḥānah bt. ʿAmr as his concubine.

✧ This section discusses Qurʾanic verses revealed about the trench and Banū Qurayẓa, including commentary on God's sending wind and unseen hosts, the believers' trials, and hypocrites' behavior, with philological explanations.

✧ Saʿd b. Muʿādh dies from his wound after the affair of Banū Qurayẓa, and the section reports Gabriel's statement about heaven's gates and the Throne shaking, as well as the grave's squeezing and elegies for him.
✧ Lists the Muslim and polytheist dead from the Trench, including six Muslims, three polytheists, and the refusal to sell Nawfal's body, then notes martyrs at Banū Qurayẓah.
✧ Records the Prophet's glad tidings of future raids on Quraysh and collects extensive poetry from the Trench and Qurayẓah by poets such as Ḍirār, Kaʿb, Ḥassān, and Hubayrah.
✧ Narrates the Khazraj's assassination of Sallām b. Abī al-Ḥuqayq in Khaybar, including the selection of the party, their entry, killing, confirmation of death, and Ḥassān's praise poem.
✧ Covers the Islam of ʿAmr b. al-ʿĀṣ and Khālid b. al-Walīd through ʿAmr's visit to the Negus and their subsequent agreement.
✧ ʿAmr b. al-ʿĀṣ travels to the Negus with Quraysh companions, encounters ʿAmr b. Umayyah al-Ḍamrī, and the Negus testifies to the Prophet's truth, leading ʿAmr to secretly embrace Islam.
✧ ʿAmr b. al-ʿĀṣ and Khālid b. al-Walīd meet and agree to embrace Islam, go to the Prophet in Madinah, pledge allegiance, and Ibn al-Zibaʿrā composes poetry about Ibn Ṭalḥah's conversion.
✧ Describes the Messenger's expedition against Banū Liḥyān to avenge al-Rajīʿ and includes Kaʿb's poetry on it.
✧ The Messenger ﷺ departs for Banū Liḥyān, appoints Ibn Umm Maktūm over Madinah, takes a misleading route, finds them alerted, advances to ʿUsfān, and returns with a supplication.
✧ Kaʿb b. Mālik's verses rebuke Banū Liḥyān for not uniting to face the Muslims, likening them to fleeing hyraxes.
✧ The expedition of Dhū Qarad recounts ʿUyaynah b. Ḥiṣn's raid on the Prophet's milch-camels, the Muslim pursuit, slain polytheists, spoils division, and related poetry.
✧ ʿUyaynah b. Ḥiṣn al-Fazārī raids the Prophet's milch-camels at al-Ghābah, and Salamah b. al-Akwaʿ warns the Muslims, initiating the pursuit in which Muḥriz b. Naḍlah is killed.
✧ The names of the Muslims' horses in the expedition of Dhū Qarad are listed, including Dhū al-Limmah, Lāḥiqah, Baʿzajah, Ḥazwah, and al-Janāḥ.
✧ Abū Qatādah kills Ḥabīb b. ʿUyaynah, ʿUkkāshah b. Miḥṣan kills Awbār and his son, and some milch-camels are recovered before the Prophet stops at Dhū Qarad.
✧ The Prophet divides one slaughtered camel per hundred men among his companions, and the wife of al-Ghifārī is told not to slaughter the she-camel she vowed.
✧ Ḥassān b. Thābit's poems on Dhū Qarad praise the Muslim horsemen, anger Saʿd b. Zayd over the attribution to al-Miqdād, and rebuke ʿUyaynah.
✧ Kaʿb b. Mālik's verses on the day of Dhū Qarad extol the Muslim horsemen's courage, generosity, and martial prowess against their enemies.
✧ Shaddād b. ʿĀriḍ al-Jushamī addresses ʿUyaynah b. Ḥiṣn, reproaching his retreat and praising the pursuing Muslim horsemen at Dhū Qarad.
✧ The expedition against Banū al-Muṣṭaliq covers its timing, cause, the conflict involving Ibn Ubayy, casualties, Juwayriyah's capture and marriage, and the slander of ʿĀʾishah.
✧ The expedition occurred in Shaʿbān of year six after a stay in Madinah, with Abū Dharr al-Ghifārī or Numaylah b. ʿAbd Allāh al-Laythī left in charge.
✧ The Messenger raided Banū al-Muṣṭaliq at al-Muraysīʿ after learning of their gathering, defeating them and taking captives, including Juwayriyah, while a Muslim killed Hishām b. Ṣubābah by mistake.
✧ An altercation over water between Jahjāh and Sinān led Ibn Ubayy to speak defiantly, prompting Qurʾānic revelation and his son's offer to kill him.
✧ ʿAlī b. Abī Ṭālib killed Mālik and his son, and ʿAbd al-Raḥmān b. ʿAwf killed a horseman named Aḥmar or Uḥaymir.
✧ Juwayriyah bt. al-Ḥārith, captured and allotted to Thābit b. Qays, was freed and married by the Prophet, leading to the release of a hundred households of her tribe.
✧ Al-Walīd b. ʿUqbah's false report about Banū al-Muṣṭaliq withholding alms prompted Qurʾanic verses on verifying news from a disobedient person.
✧ Al-Zuhrī and others narrate the slander (al-ifk) during the expedition of Banū al-Muṣṭaliq in year six, collected by Ibn Isḥāq from multiple transmitters.
✧ The Messenger ﷺ casts lots among his wives before journeys, and ʿĀʾishah is chosen to accompany him on the expedition of Banū al-Muṣṭaliq.
✧ ʿĀʾishah stays behind to search for her lost necklace, is found by Ṣafwān b. al-Muʿaṭṭal, falls ill in Madinah, and learns of the slander from Umm Misṭaḥ.
✧ The Messenger ﷺ publicly defends his family, the slander is traced to ʿAbd Allāh b. Ubayy and Ḥamnah bt. Jaḥsh, and after consulting ʿAlī and Usāmah he questions Barīrah about ʿĀʾishah.
✧ The Qurʾān reveals ʿĀʾishah's innocence, Abū Bakr restores Misṭaḥ's allowance, Ṣafwān strikes Ḥassān over his satire, and Ḥassān is compensated and flogged.

✧ The affair of al-Ḥudaybiyah at the end of year six, including the Messenger's departure, the pledge of al-Riḍwān, Quraysh sending Suhayl b. ʿAmr, witnesses to the reconciliation, the revelation of Sūrat al-Fatḥ, oppressed Muslims after the truce, and emigrant women.

✧ The Messenger ﷺ departs for ʿumrah with sacrificial animals, avoids Quraysh through a rugged route, receives envoys Budayl, Mikraz, al-Ḥulays, and ʿUrwah, and sends ʿUthmān to Makkah where he is detained.
✧ The Messenger ﷺ takes the pledge of al-Riḍwān under the tree after news of ʿUthmān's alleged killing, with al-Jadd b. Qays staying behind and Abū Sinān al-Asadī being the first to pledge.
✧ Suhayl b. ʿAmr is sent by Quraysh to negotiate peace, leading to the terms written by ʿAlī, ʿUmar's objections, and the return of Abū Jandal.
✧ The peace document is witnessed by Muslims and polytheists, after which the Messenger sacrifices, shaves, and prays for those who shaved.
✧ Sūrat al-Fatḥ is revealed during the return, confirming the pledge under the tree and foretelling the near victory from the Ḥudaybiyyah peace.
✧ Abū Baṣīr comes to Madinah, kills his escort after being handed back, and gathers oppressed Muslims at al-ʿĪṣ, prompting Quraysh to beg for their repatriation.
✧ Umm Kulthūm bt. ʿUqbah emigrates but is not returned, and ʿUrwah explains the ruling that believing women are tested and kept while dowers are exchanged.
✧ The Messenger marches to Khaybar in Muḥarram of year seven, with sections covering the journey, encampments, fighting, reconciliations, spoils, and later expulsion of the Jews.
✧ The Messenger leaves Madinah for Khaybar, appoints Numaylah over the city, and hears ʿĀmir b. al-Akwaʿ recite verses before his martyrdom there.
✧ Upon overlooking Khaybar, the Messenger supplicates for its good and seeks refuge from its evil, then the workers flee upon seeing the army.
✧ Describes the Messenger's route and encampments from Madinah to Khaybar, Ghatafān's aborted support for the Jews, and the conquest of fortresses including Nāʿim and al-Qamūṣ.
✧ Records the Messenger's prohibitions at Khaybar, the Banū Sahm's supplication, and duels in which Marḥab, Yāsir, and other champions were killed, culminating in ʿAlī's victory.
✧ Narrates the interrogation and execution of Kinānah b. al-Rabīʿ for withholding the Banū al-Naḍīr treasure.
✧ Covers the peace terms with Khaybar and Fadak, the poisoned ewe incident, the return journey, spoils-related anecdotes, marriage to Ṣafiyyah, Bilāl's watch, and victory poetry.
✧ Reports the presence of women at Khaybar, their small share of booty, and the account of a Ghifārī woman's menstruation and gift of a necklace.
✧ Lists the Muslim martyrs of Khaybar from Quraysh, the Anṣār, and allied tribes, with their tribal affiliations.
✧ Relates the conversion, death, and promised heavenly wives of al-Aswad the shepherd, a Jewish hireling who joined the Muslims at Khaybar.
✧ Tells how al-Ḥajjāj b. ʿIlāṭ deceived Quraysh to recover his wealth from Makkah, and includes poems by Ḥassān, Nājiyah, and Kaʿb on Khaybar.
✧ Details the distribution of Khaybar's lands among the Prophet ﷺ, his relatives, wives, and Companions, specifying shares, recipients, and quantities.
✧ Records the Prophet's ﷺ allotment of Khaybar wheat to his wives and certain Companions, along with his final bequests to several clans.
✧ Describes the peace agreement granting the Prophet ﷺ half of Fadak, the appointment of assessors over Khaybar, and the blood-money paid after ʿAbd Allāh b. Sahl's killing.
✧ Explains how ʿUmar expelled the Jews from Khaybar based on the Prophet's instruction that two religions should not remain in Arabia.
✧ Lists the Companions who received shares when ʿUmar divided Wādī al-Qurā among the Muslims.
✧ Covers the joy at Jaʿfar b. Abī Ṭālib's return, naming those emigrants brought back from Abyssinia, and separately listing the women emigrants.
✧ Recounts the Messenger's ﷺ embrace and his joy upon Jaʿfar b. Abī Ṭālib's arrival at Khaybar.
✧ Names the sixteen male emigrants from Abyssinia who returned with ʿAmr b. Umayyah, then lists other emigrants who returned later, perished there, or remained.
✧ Lists sixteen women Qurayshī and Arab emigrants to Abyssinia, their clans, deaths en route, and the ten children born to them there.
✧ Describes the Messenger's ﷺ compensatory ʿumra in Dhū al-Qaʿda year seven, including departure, raml, and marriage to Maymūna.
✧ The Messenger ﷺ departed from Madinah in Dhū al-Qaʿda year seven, leaving ʿUwayf b. al-Aḍbaṭ as governor, to perform the retaliatory ʿumra after Quraysh blocked him the previous year.
✧ Explains the origin of raml: the Prophet ﷺ jogged during ṭawāf to display strength before Quraysh, and Ibn Rawāḥa recited verses while leading his camel.
✧ The Prophet ﷺ married Maymūna bt. al-Ḥārith through al-ʿAbbās during the ʿumra, stayed three days, then left when Quraysh requested, consummating the marriage at Sarif.
✧ Covers the Muʾta expedition in Jumādā al-Ūlā year eight, including commanders Zayd b. Ḥāritha, Jaʿfar b. Abī Ṭālib, and ʿAbd Allāh b. Rawāḥa leading to their deaths.
✧ Dates the Muʾta expedition to Jumādā al-Ūlā of year eight, after the Messenger ﷺ remained in Madinah from Dhū al-Ḥijjah through the two Rabīʿs.
✧ The Prophet ﷺ appointed Zayd b. Ḥāritha, then Jaʿfar, then Ibn Rawāḥa as commanders of the 3,000-strong Muʾta force, and Ibn Rawāḥa expressed fear of the Fire and poetic farewell.
✧ The Muslims halted at Maʿān upon learning of Heraclius's huge army, and Ibn Rawāḥah encouraged them to seek martyrdom or victory.
✧ The Muslim army met the Byzantines at Mashārif, withdrew to Muʾtah, and fought with Zayd b. Ḥārithah carrying the banner until he was killed.
✧ Jaʿfar b. Abī Ṭālib took the banner after Zayd, hamstrung his horse, and fought until he was killed, receiving two wings in Paradise.
✧ ʿAbd Allāh b. Rawāḥah took the banner after Jaʿfar, overcame his hesitation, dismounted, and fought until he was killed.
✧ The Prophet ﷺ foretold the successive martyrdoms of Zayd, Jaʿfar, and ʿAbd Allāh b. Rawāḥah, noting the latter's slight hesitation.
✧ The Messenger ﷺ grieved for Jaʿfar, instructed that food be prepared for his family, and the army's return was met with abuse and poetical responses.
✧ The section lists the Muslims martyred at Muʾtah, including Jaʿfar, Zayd, ʿAbd Allāh b. Rawāḥah, and others from Quraysh and the Anṣār.
✧ The causes of the conquest of Makkah, including the fighting between Bakr and Khuzāʿa, Abū Sufyān's failed peace mission, and the events of the conquest.
✧ It recounts the attack by Banū Bakr on Khuzāʿa at al-Watīr with Quraysh's secret aid, breaking the truce, and the subsequent poems and appeals for help.
✧ Budayl b. Warqāʾ travels to Madinah to complain about Quraysh's backing of Banū Bakr, and Abū Sufyān discerns from camel dung that he had visited the Prophet ﷺ.
✧ Abū Sufyān's attempts in Madinah to secure reconciliation are rebuffed by his daughter, Abū Bakr, ʿUmar, and ʿAlī, and his granting of protection proves futile.
✧ The Messenger ﷺ secretly prepares for the conquest of Makkah and marches with a large force, while Ḥassān b. Thābit incites the people with verses about Khuzāʿa's slain.
✧ Ḥāṭib b. Abī Baltaʿah's letter warning Quraysh is intercepted by ʿAlī and al-Zubayr, leading to his summons, ʿUmar's rebuke, and the Qur'anic revelation concerning his case.
✧ The Messenger ﷺ departs in Ramaḍān, appoints Abū Ruhm al-Ghifārī over Madinah, encounters relatives who convert, and camps at Marr al-Ẓahrān with ten thousand Muslims.
✧ Al-ʿAbbās brings Abū Sufyān to the Prophet ﷺ, overcomes ʿUmar's objection, and after a dialogue about faith, Abū Sufyān testifies and is granted amnesty.

✧ As the Muslim tribes and the green squadron pass before him, Abū Sufyān marvels at their strength, then returns to Makkah urging surrender and declaring safety for those entering Abū Sufyān's house or the mosque.
✧ At Dhū Ṭuwā the Prophet ﷺ halted in humility, and Abū Quḥāfah was brought to convert to Islam.
✧ The Prophet ﷺ dispatched al-Zubayr and Saʿd b. ʿUbādah into Makkah, then replaced Saʿd with ʿAlī after his alarming war cry.
✧ Khālid, Abū ʿUbaydah, and the Prophet ﷺ entered Makkah by different routes, and at al-Khandamah Khālid's forces repelled Ṣafwān, ʿIkrimah, and Suhayl.
✧ War cries of the Muhājirūn, Khazraj, and Aws are given, alongside the Prophet's ﷺ order to kill certain named individuals, including ʿAbd Allāh b. Saʿd.
✧ Names and reasons are listed for those the Prophet ﷺ ordered killed, and Umm Hāniʾ's protection of two Makhzūmī men is honored by the Prophet ﷺ.
✧ The Prophet ﷺ circumambulated the Kaʿbah, broke its wooden dove, and addressed Quraysh from its door about monotheism and forgiveness.
✧ The Prophet ﷺ restored the Kaʿbah key to ʿUthmān b. Ṭalḥah and ordered the effacement of images inside the House.
✧ Ibn ʿUmar inquired where the Prophet ﷺ prayed inside the Kaʿbah, and the Prophet ﷺ revealed his knowledge of Abū Sufyān and others' remarks.
✧ It recounts the first blood-money the Messenger paid for Junaydab b. al-Akwaʿ, his reassurance to the Anṣār, the falling of the idols, and Fuḍālah b. ʿUmayr's foiled attempt.
✧ It covers the Messenger's grant of safety to Ṣafwān b. Umayyah via ʿUmayr b. Wahb, and the conversions of ʿIkrimah, Ṣafwān, and Ibn al-Zibaʿrā, along with Hubayrah's rejection.
✧ It gives the number of Muslims at the conquest as ten thousand and presents poems by Ḥassān b. Thābit, Anas b. Zunaym, Budayl, Bujayr, ʿAbbās b. Mirdās, Jaʿdah, and Bujayd.
✧ It recounts Khālid b. al-Walīd's expedition to Banū Jadhīmah, the Messenger's injunctions and anger, Khālid's excuse, and the subsequent conflict and reconciliation.
✧ It narrates the Messenger sending Khālid as a caller, his attack on Banū Jadhīmah despite their laying down arms, the killing of captives, and the Messenger's disavowal of his action.
✧ It describes the Messenger's anger at Khālid's deed, his dispatch of ʿAlī to compensate the victims fully, and his public declaration of innocence three times.
✧ It gives Khālid's excuse that ʿAbd Allāh b. Ḥudhāfah ordered him to fight, and the Messenger's rebuke of Khālid for dishonoring his companions.
✧ It relates the background conflict between Quraysh and Banū Jadhīmah over a merchant's property, their eventual peace, and includes several poems on the affair.
✧ Khālid b. al-Walīd is sent to destroy the idol al-ʿUzzā at Nakhla, where its Sulamī keeper curses him before he demolishes it and returns to the Prophet ﷺ.
✧ The expedition of Ḥunayn covers Hawāzin's gathering, the battle, the siege of al-Ṭāʾif, and subsequent division of spoils and reconciliation with the Anṣār.
✧ Mālik b. ʿAwf gathers Hawāzin and Thaqīf at Awṭās with their families and wealth, ignoring Durayd b. al-Ṣimmah's advice against this.
✧ Mālik b. ʿAwf's scouts see white riders on piebald horses, while ʿAbd Allāh b. Abī Ḥadrad spies on Hawāzin and Ṣafwān b. Umayyah lends the Prophet ﷺ coats of mail.
✧ The Messenger ﷺ departs with twelve thousand men to meet Hawāzin, leaving ʿAttāb b. Asīd over Makkah, and ʿAbbās b. Mirdās recites war poetry.
✧ On the way to Ḥunayn, some Muslims ask the Prophet ﷺ to create a sacred tree like Dhāt Anwāṭ, and he rebukes them for echoing the Israelites.
✧ At the valley of Ḥunayn, Hawāzin ambush the Muslims at dawn, most flee, but the Prophet ﷺ stands firm calling to them with a small group of Companions.
✧ During the Muslim rout, Abū Sufyān b. Ḥarb and Kalada b. al-Ḥanbal gloat, while Ṣafwān b. Umayyah rebukes Kalada, and Ḥassān satirizes him.
✧ Shaybah b. ʿUthmān abandons his resolve to kill the Prophet when his heart is overcome, followed by accounts of the Muslim rout at Ḥunayn, al-ʿAbbās's rallying call, and the counterattack.
✧ ʿAlī and an Anṣārī disable the Hawāzin standard-bearer's camel, and the narrative includes Umm Sulaym's encounter with the Prophet and Abū Qatādah's claim to spoils.
✧ Jubayr b. Muṭʿim recounts seeing something like black ants descending from the sky, which he took to be angels aiding the Muslims before the enemy's defeat.
✧ The polytheists are routed, a Muslim woman extols God's cavalry over al-Lāt's, and seventy Thaqīf men, including ʿUthmān b. ʿAbd Allāh, are killed under their banner.
✧ A slain uncircumcised Christian slave causes a rumor that Thaqīf are uncircumcised, which al-Mughīrah b. Shuʿbah suppresses, and ʿAbbās b. Mirdās's poem satirizes Qārib's flight.
✧ Rabīʿah b. Rufayʿ kills the elderly Durayd b. al-Ṣimmah, who instructs him on the fatal blow, and ʿAmrah bt. Durayd laments her father's death in verse.
✧ Abū ʿĀmir al-Ashʿarī is killed by an arrow from Salamah b. Durayd at Awṭās, after which Abū Mūsā al-Ashʿarī takes the banner and routs the enemy.
✧ Mālik b. ʿAwf holds a mountain pass as his people retreat, identifies the approaching cavalry, and is dislodged by al-Zubayr b. al-ʿAwwām's charge, with appended poetry on the flight.
✧ The Messenger ﷺ forbade killing children, women, and hired servants, and recognized his foster sister al-Shaymāʾ bt. al-Ḥārith, giving her provision and returning her to her people.

✧ It names the Muslims martyred at Ḥunayn, including Ayman b. ʿUbayd, Yazīd b. Zamaʿa, Surāqa b. al-Ḥārith, and Abū ʿĀmir al-Ashʿarī, and includes poems by Bujayr, ʿAbbās b. Mirdās, and others about the battle.
✧ The remnant of Thaqīf arrived at al-Ṭāʾif and shut the city gates, preparing to fight the Muslims.
✧ ʿUrwah b. Masʿūd and Ghaylān b. Salamah missed Ḥunayn and the siege of al-Ṭāʾif because they were at Jurash learning siegecraft including testudos, mangonels, and ḍubūr.

✧ The Messenger ﷺ marched from Ḥunayn to al-Ṭāʾif, demolished Mālik b. ʿAwf's fortress, renamed al-Dayyiqah as al-Yusrā, and besieged the town for about twenty nights while Kaʿb b. Mālik and Kinānah b. ʿAbd Yālīl exchanged poems.
✧ The Messenger ﷺ was the first in Islam to shoot a mangonel, and when a testudo assault failed he cut Thaqīf's vines but departed after ʿUmar announced the withdrawal.
✧ Thaqīf seized the family of Marwān b. Qays, who captured Ubayy b. Mālik al-Qushayrī, and al-Ḍaḥḥāk b. Sufyān intervened to secure their release, commemorated in his poem.
✧ It names twelve Muslim martyrs at al-Ṭāʾif—seven from Quraysh, four from the Anṣār, and one from Banū Layth—followed by Bujayr b. Zuhayr's poem on Ḥunayn and al-Ṭāʾif.
✧ It recounts the Messenger's ﷺ departure from al-Ṭāʾif to al-Jiʿrānah with Hawāzin captives and his prayer for Thaqīf's guidance.
✧ It narrates the return of Hawāzin captives at al-Jiʿrānah, the conversion and appointment of Mālik b. ʿAwf, and his subsequent raids on Thaqīf.
✧ It describes the Messenger's ﷺ urging the return of spoils down to a needle and thread, with the refusal of ʿAqīl b. Abī Ṭālib's wife to keep one.
✧ It lists gifts of one hundred or fewer camels to nobles to reconcile their hearts, including Abū Sufyān b. Ḥarb, and the appeasement of ʿAbbās b. Mirdās.
✧ It lists recipients of Ḥunayn spoils by clan, records the Messenger's ﷺ reply about Juʿayl b. Surāqah, Dhū al-Khuwayṣirah's objection, and Ḥassān's reproachful verses about the Anṣār's deprivation.
✧ It recounts how the Anṣār resented being excluded from gifts, and the Messenger ﷺ appeased them in an address affirming their merit and his fellowship with them.
✧ It covers the Messenger's ﷺ ʿumrah from al-Jiʿrānah, including his appointment of ʿAttāb b. Asīd over Makkah and the timing of the ʿumrah.
✧ It narrates the Messenger's ﷺ ʿumrah from al-Jiʿrānah, his detention of remaining spoils at Majannah, and appointment of ʿAttāb b. Asīd with Muʿādh b. Jabal over Makkah.
✧ Covers the timing of the Prophet's ʿumrah in Dhū al-Qaʿdah, the ḥajj leadership of ʿAttāb b. Asīd, and the repentance and poems of Kaʿb b. Zuhayr.
✧ Relates the preparations, incidents, and aftermath of the Tabūk expedition, including the cases of those who stayed behind and the destruction of the Mosque of Ḍirār.
✧ Describes the Prophet's ﷺ command to prepare for the Byzantine expedition during severe heat and hardship, openly stating the destination.
✧ Recounts al-Jadd b. Qays's request to remain behind and the Qur'anic revelation concerning his temptation.
✧ Reports the hypocrites' discouragement from jihād, the Qur'anic response, and the burning of Suwaylim's house where they gathered.
✧ Tells of the Messenger's ﷺ urging for contributions and ʿUthmān b. ʿAffān's exceptional spending of one thousand dinars.
✧ Describes the seven needy companions known as the weepers who lacked mounts and were provided with a camel by Ibn Yāmīn.
✧ Mentions the bedouin excuse-makers who were not excused and the sincere Muslims who stayed behind without doubt, including Kaʿb b. Mālik.

✧ The Prophet ﷺ left Madinah, appointed deputies, and dealt with the staying behind of the hypocrites and false rumors about ʿAlī b. Abī Ṭālib, while Abū Khaythamah repented and rejoined the expedition.
✧ At al-Ḥijr the Prophet ﷺ commanded the Muslims to drink no water and go out only with companions; two men disobeyed and were afflicted, and later rain came through supplication.
✧ The Messenger's she-camel went astray, and the hypocrite Ibn al-Luṣayt mocked his prophetic knowledge, so the Prophet ﷺ revealed its location and ʿUmārah b. Ḥazm expelled him.
✧ Abū Dharr lagged behind when his camel delayed him, then walked alone to join the Prophet ﷺ, who said he would walk, die, and be raised alone, as later fulfilled at al-Rabadhah.

✧ Hypocrites including Wadīʿah b. Thābit and Mukhashshin b. Ḥumayyir discouraged the Muslims before Tabūk, and Qurʾān was revealed about their idle talk and jesting, with Mukhashshin renamed ʿAbd al-Raḥmān.
✧ At Tabūk, Yuḥannā b. Ruʾbah of Aylah and the people of Jarbāʾ and Adhruḥ made peace and gave jizyah, and the Prophet ﷺ wrote them a guarantee of security for ships and caravans.
✧ Khālid b. al-Walīd captured Ukaydir b. ʿAbd al-Malik of Dūmah while hunting wild cows, and the Prophet ﷺ spared his blood and made peace with him on payment of jizyah.
✧ At Wādī al-Mushaqqaq, hypocrites drew its scant water despite the Prophet's prohibition, and after cursing them, he prayed over the trickle and it burst forth abundantly.
✧ Relates the death and burial of Dhū al-Bijādayn during Tabūk, the Prophet’s prayer over him, the origin of his name, and an encounter with Abū Ruhm about those who stayed behind.
✧ Describes the Prophet’s order to demolish and burn the Mosque of Ḍirār after returning from Tabūk and lists its twelve builders.
✧ Enumerates the mosques of the Messenger between Madinah and Tabūk, naming each location.
✧ Reports the Prophet’s prohibition on speaking to the three Muslims left behind—Kaʿb b. Mālik, Murārah b. al-Rabīʿ, and Hilāl b. Umayyah—and his acceptance of excuses from the hypocrites.
✧ Kaʿb b. Mālik narrates his failure to join Tabūk, his truthful confession, and the fifty-night boycott until God’s acceptance.
✧ Describes the announcement of God’s acceptance of the three men’s repentance after fifty nights, Kaʿb’s joy and gift of his garments, and the Qur’anic verses revealed about them.
✧ Covers the delegation of Thaqīf in Ramaḍān year nine, including ʿUrwah b. Masʿūd’s conversion, the sending of emissaries, Bilāl’s hospitality, and the Prophet’s charge and letter to them.
✧ ʿUrwah b. Masʿūd converts and returns to Thaqīf to call them to Islam, but they shoot arrows at him and kill him; he rejoices in martyrdom.
✧ Thaqīf deliberates sending a delegation to the Messenger ﷺ after ʿUrwah's killing, led by ʿAbd Yālīl with five companions, and negotiates terms including initial requests about al-Lāt and prayer.
✧ Bilāl brings the Thaqīf delegation their pre-dawn and evening meals during Ramaḍān, explaining the Prophet's ﷺ practice of delaying saḥūr and hastening ifṭār.
✧ The Messenger ﷺ instructs ʿUthmān b. Abī al-ʿĀṣ to shorten prayers and consider the weakest, and sends Abū Sufyān and al-Mughīrah to demolish the idol al-Lāt and settle debts from its wealth.
✧ The Prophet ﷺ writes Thaqīf a letter protecting the acacia trees and game of Wajj, prescribing flogging and seizure for violators, written by Khālid b. Saʿīd.
✧ Abū Bakr leads the pilgrimage in year nine, and the Prophet ﷺ sends ʿAlī to proclaim the opening of Barāʾah, annulling treaties with polytheists and establishing new rulings for pilgrimage.
✧ Ḥassān b. Thābit's poems enumerate the expeditions and praise the Anṣār's steadfastness, recounting battles from Badr to Tabūk and affirming their loyalty.
✧ The year nine is named the Year of Delegations because after the conquest of Makkah and Tabūk, Arab tribes sent delegations to the Messenger ﷺ, marking widespread submission to Islam.
✧ After the conquest of Makkah, Tabūk, and Thaqīf's submission, delegations of Arabs came to the Prophet ﷺ from every direction, and the year was called the Year of Delegations.
✧ The Arabs' acceptance of Islam followed Quraysh's submission after the conquest of Makkah, fulfilling the Quranic prophecy of entering religion in throngs.
✧ The delegation of Banū Tamīm vied in oratory and poetry with Thābit b. Qays and Ḥassān b. Thābit, then submitted, prompting revelation of Sūrat al-Ḥujurāt.
✧ ʿĀmir b. al-Ṭufayl planned with Arbad b. Qays to assassinate the Prophet ﷺ during their delegation's visit, but Arbad failed to strike.
✧ In response to the Prophet's ﷺ supplication against him, ʿĀmir b. al-Ṭufayl died of a plague in his neck at a Salūlī woman's house.
✧ Arbad b. Qays and his camel were killed by a thunderbolt, and Quranic verses were revealed concerning him and ʿĀmir, with Labīd mourning Arbad in elegiac poetry.
✧ Ḍimām b. Thaʿlabah came as envoy from Banū Saʿd b. Bakr, questioned the Prophet ﷺ about Islam's obligations, converted, and successfully called his people to Islam.
✧ Al-Jārūd b. ʿAmr, a Christian, came in the delegation of ʿAbd al-Qays, accepted Islam after the Prophet ﷺ guaranteed divine guidance, and later opposed the riddah.
✧ The delegation of Banū Ḥanīfah included Musaylimah the Liar, who later apostatized, claimed prophethood as a partner, and composed rhymed prose imitating the Quran.
✧ Zayd al-Khayl came in the delegation of Ṭayyiʾ, accepted Islam, was renamed Zayd al-Khayr, granted lands, and died of fever on his journey home.
✧ ʿAdī b. Ḥātim, a Christian chief of Ṭayyiʾ, fled to Syria out of hatred for the Prophet, leaving behind his daughter.
✧ The Prophet's cavalry captured Ḥātim's daughter, but he released her honorably and sent her to her brother in Syria.
✧ Ḥātim's daughter advised ʿAdī to join the Prophet quickly, arguing he would gain excellence if a prophet and not be humbled if a king.
✧ ʿAdī came to the Prophet in Madinah, observed his humility, heard his prophecies about future prosperity and conquests, and became a Muslim.
✧ Farwah b. Musayk al-Murādī came to the Prophet after defecting from the kings of Kindah, was appointed over Murād, Zubayd, and Madhḥij, and sent with Khālid b. Saʿīd for ṣadaqah.
✧ ʿAmr b. Maʿdīkarib came with Banū Zubayd and became Muslim, but later apostatized after the Prophet's death and criticized Farwah's rule.
✧ Al-Ashʿath b. Qays came with eighty Kindah riders, removed their silk adornments at the Prophet's command, claimed descent from Ākil al-Murār, and was corrected about the Prophet's own lineage.
✧ Surad b. ʿAbd Allāh al-Azdī converts to Islam, is appointed over his people, fights the people of Jurash, and the Jurash delegation later embraces Islam.
✧ Envoys from the kings of Ḥimyar announce their acceptance of Islam, and the Prophet ﷺ writes them a letter outlining alms, jizyah, and the mission of Muʿādh b. Jabal.
✧ The Prophet ﷺ charges Muʿādh b. Jabal to make things easy when sent to Yemen, and Muʿādh answers a woman's question about a husband's right.
✧ Farwah b. ʿAmr al-Judhāmī, a Byzantine governor, converts to Islam, is imprisoned, recites poetry, and is crucified by the Byzantines.
✧ Khālid b. al-Walīd is sent to Banū al-Ḥārith b. Kaʿb; they convert, their delegation meets the Prophet ﷺ, and ʿAmr b. Ḥazm is dispatched with a covenant.
✧ Rifāʿah b. Zayd al-Judhāmī converts during the truce of al-Ḥudaybiyah, carries the Prophet's ﷺ letter to his people, and they accept Islam.
✧ The delegation of Hamdān, including Mālik b. Namaṭ, visits the Prophet ﷺ after Tabūk, and he grants them a letter over their lands.
✧ The Prophet ﷺ dreams about Musaylimah al-Ḥanafī and al-Aswad al-ʿAnsī, speaks of false claimants, and exchanges letters with Musaylimah.
✧ Reports the Prophet's dream of two gold bracelets, which he interpreted as the false prophets Musaylimah b. Ḥabīb in al-Yamāmah and al-Aswad b. Kaʿb al-ʿAnsī in Ṣanʿāʾ.
✧ Records the Prophet's prediction that thirty dajjāls would appear before the Hour and lists the commanders and collectors he sent for alms across various regions.
✧ Contains Musaylimah's letter claiming partnership in prophethood and the Prophet's reply rebuking him as "the liar," along with his refusal to kill the messengers.
✧ Covers the Prophet's preparations, appointment of Abū Dujānah over Madinah, instructions to ʿĀʾishah during her menstruation, ʿAlī's meeting upon returning from Yemen, and the Farewell Sermon.
✧ Describes the Prophet's departure for the pilgrimage with five nights left in Dhū al-Qaʿdah and his appointment of Abū Dujānah al-Sāʿidī, or alternatively Sibāʿ b. ʿUrfuṭah, over Madinah.
✧ Relates the Prophet's instruction to ʿĀʾishah not to weep over her menstruation, her performing all rites except circumambulation, and his command for his wives to exit iḥrām with an ʿumrah.
✧ Describes ʿAlī's return from Yemen, his conflict with the Prophet over exiting iḥrām, the Prophet's making him a partner in his sacrificial animal, and the troops' complaint about his harshness.
✧ Presents the Farewell Sermon at ʿArafah, including declarations of sanctity, abolition of usury and blood feuds, rights of women, and the teachings on standing places during the pilgrimage.
✧ The Prophet ﷺ appointed Usāmah b. Zayd to lead an expedition to Syria, commanding him to raid al-Balqāʾ and al-Dārūm in Palestine.
✧ This section covers the Prophet's dispatch of envoys to various kings, preceded by his reminder about the disciples' disagreement over Jesus.
✧ The Prophet ﷺ reminded his companions not to differ as the disciples did, recounting how Jesus' distant envoys became sluggish until God made each speak the language of his assigned nation.
✧ It lists the Prophet's envoys and their royal recipients, including Diḥyah to Caesar, ʿAbd Allāh b. Ḥudhāfah to Chosroes, and others, alongside an account of Jesus' envoys.
✧ This heading summarizes the Prophet's expeditions and missions, including detachments led by Ghālib, Zayd, ʿAbd Allāh b. Rawāḥah, and others against various tribes.
✧ It enumerates twenty-seven expeditions in which the Prophet personally participated, noting he fought in nine of them, and lists thirty-eight missions and detachments.
✧ Ghālib b. ʿAbd Allāh al-Laythī's raid on Banū al-Mulawwaḥ at al-Kadīd, including the capture of Ibn al-Barṣāʾ, a flood that hindered pursuit, and the Muslims' watchword 'amit, amit'.
✧ Zayd b. Ḥārithah's expedition against Judhām in response to the attack on Diḥyah b. Khalīfah, involving the killing of al-Hunayd and his son and subsequent negotiations with Rifāʿah b. Zayd.
✧ Zayd b. Ḥārithah’s punitive raid against Banū Fazārah at Wādī al-Qurā, his severe treatment of the old woman Umm Qirfah, and the captives taken.
✧ ʿAbd Allāh b. Rawāḥah’s expedition to Khaybar, where al-Yasīr b. Rizām was lured out and killed along with his Jewish companions.
✧ ʿAbd Allāh b. ʿAtīk’s expedition to Khaybar, in which Abū Rāfiʿ b. Abī al-Ḥuqayq was killed.
✧ ʿAbd Allāh b. Unays’s solo mission to assassinate Khālid b. Sufyān b. Nubayḥ al-Hudhalī, and his receipt of a staff from the Prophet ﷺ.
✧ Ghālib b. ʿAbd Allāh al-Kalbī’s raid on Banū Murrah, where Usāmah b. Zayd killed a man after he had professed Islam.
✧ ʿAmr b. al-ʿĀṣ’s expedition to Dhāt al-Salāsil, his reinforcement by Abū ʿUbaydah, and accounts of Abū Bakr’s counsel and ʿAwf b. Mālik’s camel.
✧ Ibn Abī Ḥadrad’s expedition to Baṭn Iḍam, the killing of ʿĀmir b. al-Aḍbaṭ by Muḥallim b. Jaththāmah, and the subsequent dispute over blood-money.
✧ Ibn Abī Ḥadrad’s mission to gather intelligence on Rifāʿah b. Qays al-Jushamī, who was encamped at al-Ghābah to rally Qays against the Prophet ﷺ.
✧ The Muslims ambush a settlement, kill Rifāʿah b. Qays, drive off camels and sheep, and Ibn Abī Ḥadrad receives thirteen camels toward his marriage.
✧ ʿAbd al-Raḥmān b. ʿAwf is dispatched to Dūmat al-Jandal, and ʿAbd Allāh b. ʿUmar recalls the Messenger's admonitions on virtues and societal vices.
✧ The Messenger ﷺ turbans ʿAbd al-Raḥmān b. ʿAwf with a black cotton turban, instructs him on proper conduct, and gives him the banner for the expedition.
✧ Abū ʿUbaydah b. al-Jarrāḥ leads a party to the seacoast where dates run out, but God provides a sea creature that sustains them until they return.
✧ ʿAmr b. Umayyah al-Ḍamrī is sent to kill Abū Sufyān in Makkah, aborts the attempt, kills a man he mistakenly meets, and captures a Quraysh spy on his way back.
✧ Zayd b. Ḥārithah is sent to Madyan, captures prisoners from Mīnāʾ, and the Messenger ﷺ orders that mothers and children not be sold separately.
✧ Sālim b. ʿUmayr kills the elderly poet Abū ʿAfak for his satirical verses against Islam after the Messenger ﷺ asks who will deal with him.
✧ ʿUmayr b. ʿAdī al-Khiṭmī kills ʿAṣmāʾ bt. Marwān for her anti-Islamic poetry, which leads to the open acceptance of Islam by men of Banū Khaṭmah.
✧ Thumāmah b. Uthāl al-Ḥanafī is captured by the Messenger's cavalry, treated well, and after release converts to Islam, then enforces a food blockade on Makkah until the Prophet ﷺ lifts it.
✧ ʿAlqamah b. Mujazziz is sent in pursuit of raiders after Waqqāṣ b. Mujazziz's death, and his deputy ʿAbd Allāh b. Ḥudhāfah jests about obedience by ordering men toward a fire.
✧ Kurz b. Jābir is dispatched after Bajalī men who killed the Prophet's slave Yasār, who had been assigned to tend milch-camels.

✧ The Bajalīs, after recovering from illness by drinking camel milk and urine, murder herdsman Yasār and drive off camels, and upon capture Kurz brings them for exemplary punishment by amputation and blinding.
✧ ʿAlī b. Abī Ṭālib is sent on an expedition to Yemen, raiding twice, with command precedence over Khālid b. al-Walīd if their armies meet.
✧ Usāmah b. Zayd is sent as commander to Syria, with orders to raid al-Balqāʾ and al-Dārūm in Palestine, in the last detachment dispatched by the Messenger ﷺ.

✧ The Prophet's ﷺ final illness begins after a night visit to al-Baqīʿ seeking forgiveness, where he chooses meeting his Lord over worldly treasures, and he receives permission to be nursed in ʿĀʾishah's house.

✧ This section lists the Mothers of the Believers, including his marriages to Khadījah, ʿĀʾishah, Sawdah, Zaynab bt. Jaḥsh, Umm Salamah, Ḥafṣah, Umm Ḥabībah, Juwayriyah, Ṣafiyyah, Maymūnah, and Zaynab bt. Khuzaymah.
✧ Lists the nine wives of the Prophet ﷺ with their names and lineages.
✧ Describes the Prophet's ﷺ first marriage to Khadījah bt. Khuwaylid, her previous husbands, and children.
✧ Narrates the marriage and consummation with ʿĀʾishah bt. Abī Bakr, including her age and dowry.
✧ Details the marriage to Sawdah bt. Zamʿah, including her guardian, dowry, and previous husband.
✧ Records the marriage to Zaynab bt. Jaḥsh after her divorce from Zayd b. Ḥārithah.
✧ Relates the marriage to Umm Salamah, with her dowry and children from her previous husband.
✧ Describes the marriage to Ḥafṣah bt. ʿUmar, her dowry, and previous husband.
✧ Covers the marriage to Umm Ḥabībah in Abyssinia, including the Negus paying her dower.
✧ The Prophet ﷺ married Juwayriyah bt. al-Ḥārith after she was taken captive from Banū al-Muṣṭaliq, either by paying her ransom, marrying her, or purchasing and freeing her.
✧ The Prophet ﷺ married Ṣafiyyah bt. Ḥuyayy after capturing her at Khaybar and held a wedding feast of sawīq and dates.
✧ The Prophet ﷺ married Maymūnah bt. al-Ḥārith through al-ʿAbbās, who paid her dower, with reports that she offered herself to him.
✧ The Prophet ﷺ married Zaynab bt. Khuzaymah, called Umm al-Masākīn, for a bride-price of four hundred dirhams, and she died before him.
✧ During the Prophet's final illness in ʿĀʾishah's house, he addressed the community, dispatched Usāmah's expedition, gave testament regarding the Anṣār, and Abū Bakr led prayers.
✧ The Prophet ﷺ praised Abū Bakr from the pulpit, indicating his choice of the hereafter and ordering that all mosque doors be closed except Abū Bakr's.
✧ The Prophet ﷺ urged the dispatch of Usāmah's expedition despite criticisms of his young leadership, and Usāmah camped at al-Jurf until the Prophet's death.
✧ The Prophet ﷺ instructed the Muhājirūn to treat the Anṣār well, then his illness worsened and his wives administered a ludud remedy against his will.

✧ Usāmah b. Zayd describes the Messenger ﷺ, rendered speechless in his final illness, gesturing in supplication over him, followed by ʿĀʾishah’s account of his last words choosing the Highest Companion.
✧ In his final illness the Messenger ﷺ ordered Abū Bakr to lead the prayer, and when ʿUmar initially led it, he insisted that only Abū Bakr do so.

✧ On Monday the Messenger ﷺ appeared during the dawn prayer, then withdrew and died later that day, with accounts of his last public speech, the exchange between al-ʿAbbās and ʿAlī, and the recognition of his death.
✧ ʿĀʾishah relates that shortly before his death the Messenger ﷺ used a tooth-stick she had softened for him, then became heavy in her lap and passed away.
✧ ʿUmar denied the Messenger’s death from the pulpit, but Abū Bakr confirmed it by reciting Qurʾān 3:144, bringing the people to acceptance.
✧ This section covers the gathering at the Saqīfah of Banū Sāʿidah after the Prophet’s death, the counsel of Ibn ʿAwf to ʿUmar, and the speeches of ʿUmar and Abū Bakr at the pledge of allegiance.
✧ After the Messenger ﷺ died, the Anṣār gathered around Saʿd b. ʿUbādah at the Saqīfah while ʿAlī, al-Zubayr, and Ṭalḥah stayed in Fāṭimah’s house, and the rest of the Muhājirūn went to Abū Bakr.
✧ ʿAbd al-Raḥmān b. ʿAwf advises ʿUmar to delay warning the people about those questioning Abū Bakr’s pledge until they return to Madinah, where his words will be understood.
✧ ʿUmar recounts the events at the Saqīfah of Banū Sāʿidah, including his own statements about stoning and the danger of unconsulted pledges, leading to Abū Bakr's election.
✧ ʿUmar publicly retracts his earlier denial of the Prophet's death, declares Abū Bakr the best successor, and calls for the community's allegiance.
✧ Abū Bakr delivers his inaugural sermon declaring his accountability for right and wrong, and ʿUmar later explains the verse that motivated his initial denial.
✧ Details cover those who washed the Prophet, the manner of washing and shrouding, his burial and the prayer over him, and the subsequent trial of the Muslims.
✧ ʿAlī b. Abī Ṭālib, al-ʿAbbās, his sons, Usāmah b. Zayd, and Shuqrān wash the Messenger's body while ʿAlī supports him against his chest.
✧ The washers are guided by a mysterious voice to keep the Prophet's shirt on while they pour water and rub him through the cloth.
✧ The Messenger is shrouded in three garments, and al-ʿAbbās arranges for Abū Ṭalḥah to dig a laḥd grave after a divine selection.
✧ After disagreement over the burial place, Abū Bakr cites the Prophet's saying that prophets are buried where they die, and he is buried under his bed after group prayers.
✧ ʿĀʾishah narrates the burial on Wednesday night, and ʿAlī b. Abī Ṭālib, al-Faḍl b. ʿAbbās, Qutham b. ʿAbbās, and the freedman Shuqrān descended into the grave, with Shuqrān burying a velvet cloak.
✧ Al-Mughīrah b. Shuʿbah claims to be the last to touch the Prophet by throwing his ring into the grave, but ʿAlī b. Abī Ṭālib calls him a liar and identifies Qutham b. ʿAbbās as the last.
✧ After the Prophet's death the Muslims were severely tried, with apostasy and turmoil until God united them under Abū Bakr, and Ḥassān b. Thābit composed several elegies lamenting his death.
